title: Affine geometric stalks at a separable closed point
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ a scheme locally of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], of pure dimension $d\in\mathbb N$ [def-weil-pure-dimension]. Let $x\in C$ be closed, with residue field $F=\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field] finite separable over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Let $K/k$ be an algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and $y\in C_K=C\times_k\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-fibre-product] a point over $x$. Set $A=\mathcal O_{C,x}$, $B=\mathcal O_{C_K,y}$ and let $\mathfrak m,\mathfrak n$ be their unique maximal ideals. For every affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}S$ of $x$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the algebra $S$ is finitely generated over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], the prime $\mathfrak p$ corresponding to $x$ is maximal, $S/\mathfrak p=F$ compatibly with $k$, and the germ map identifies $S_{\mathfrak p}=A$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The base change $U_K$ is the open inverse image of $U$ in $C_K$, compatibly with projections, and is $\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_kK)$, with tensor product as in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The point $y$ corresponds to a maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $S\otimes_kK$ with structural residue field $K$. There is a $k$-embedding $\iota:F\hookrightarrow K$ for which
$$\mathfrak q=\ker(S\otimes_kK\longrightarrow K),\qquad s\otimes\lambda\longmapsto\iota(\bar s)\lambda,$$
and the germ map identifies $B=(S\otimes_kK)_{\mathfrak q}$, compatibly with $A\to B$ and the maps on residue fields. The rings $A,B$ are Noetherian local [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; $A$ is essentially of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra] and has Krull dimension $d$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. The germ identifications induce isomorphisms of the maximal-ideal-adic completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] $\widehat A\cong\widehat{S_{\mathfrak p}}$ and $\widehat B\cong\widehat{(S\otimes_kK)_{\mathfrak q}}$. The local map $A\to B$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], with $\mathfrak mB=\mathfrak n$ and $B/\mathfrak mB=K$. Quotient rings and algebra maps use [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient].

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}S$ containing $x$. Apply the affine-pairs characterization of locally finite type to $U$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k$: $S$ is finitely generated over $k$. Since $x$ is closed, its corresponding prime $\mathfrak p$ is maximal: any prime containing it is a specialization of $x$ in $U$, hence is $x$. The affine-open stalk theorem identifies $S_{\mathfrak p}$ with $A$ by $s/u\mapsto s_x/u_x$. The prime-residue-field theorem identifies the residue field with the fraction field of $S/\mathfrak p$; since this quotient is already a field, it is $F$, with the structural $k$-map. These identifications are induced by the germ and quotient maps.

Use the open-fibre-product lemma with $V=U$, $W=\operatorname{Spec}K$ and base open $\operatorname{Spec}k$. It identifies $U_K$ with the inverse image of $U$ in $C_K$, compatibly with both projections. The affine fibre-product theorem identifies this open with $\operatorname{Spec}T$, where $T=S\otimes_kK$, and the maps with $s\mapsto s\otimes1$ and $\lambda\mapsto1\otimes\lambda$. Thus $y$ corresponds to a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $T$ contracting to $\mathfrak p$. The affine-open stalk theorem gives $B=T_{\mathfrak q}$ by its germ map. Under these germ identifications the local map is $s/u\mapsto(s\otimes1)/(u\otimes1)$: the equality holds first for sections by the projection formula just specified, then for fractions because ring maps preserve inverses.

The tensor-quotient isomorphism and tensor universal property give $T/\mathfrak pT\cong F\otimes_kK$, with $[s\otimes\lambda]\mapsto\bar s\otimes\lambda$. More explicitly, apply the tensor-quotient theorem to $S\to T$, then identify $T\otimes_S(S/\mathfrak p)$ with $(S/\mathfrak p)\otimes_kK$ by $(s\otimes\lambda)\otimes\bar a\mapsto\overline{sa}\otimes\lambda$, inverse $\bar a\otimes\lambda\mapsto(1\otimes\lambda)\otimes\bar a$; tensor balancing verifies both inverses. Because $F/k$ is finite separable and $K$ is algebraically closed, the separable-tensor lemma identifies this quotient with a finite product of copies of $K$. A prime of this product has quotient $K$: in the domain quotient the orthogonal coordinate idempotents are $0$ or $1$, their sum is $1$, and exactly one is $1$; the kernel is precisely the elements whose surviving coordinate is zero. Apply this to $\mathfrak q/\mathfrak pT$. Consequently $\mathfrak q$ is maximal and $T/\mathfrak q\cong K$ as a $K$-algebra. Restrict $T\to T/\mathfrak q\cong K$ to $S$ to obtain $\iota:S/\mathfrak p=F\to K$. It is a $k$-embedding, since a unital field homomorphism is injective. The same map sends $s\otimes\lambda$ to $\iota(\bar s)\lambda$, so its kernel is exactly $\mathfrak q$. The prime-residue-field theorem identifies $\kappa(y)$ with this quotient because $\mathfrak q$ is maximal; the structural map $K\to\kappa(y)$ is the specified isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0C4Y (lemma-change-fields-flat), affine proof and residue-fibre description; separable tensor decomposition as in Tag 0FD1 (lemma-baby-stein), via the existing separable-tensor lemma

proof.text: Apply the separable-evaluation local-base-change lemma to the finitely generated algebra $S$, its maximal ideal $\mathfrak p$, the given finite separable field $F/k$, and the embedding $\iota$ just obtained. Its evaluation kernel is precisely the prime representing $y$, so its local map is the actual map $A\to B$ from step 2. It gives Noetherian local $A,B$, faithful flatness, $\mathfrak mB=\mathfrak qB=\mathfrak n$, and $B/\mathfrak mB=K$. Its residue formula sends the class of $(s\otimes\lambda)/v$ to $\iota(\bar s)\lambda/\epsilon(v)$; hence the residue map $F\to K$ is exactly $\iota$. Also $A$ is essentially of finite type by its displayed localization of the finite type $k$-algebra $S$, which is precisely the definition of that notion.

Pure dimension means all irreducible components of $C$ have dimension $d$. Apply the equidimensional-open local-dimension lemma with $Y=C$ and $O=C$: $\dim_x C=d$. Open-subspace invariance gives $\dim_x U=d$. Since $S$ is finitely generated and $\mathfrak p$ is maximal, the closed-point local-dimension theorem gives $\dim S_{\mathfrak p}=\dim_x U=d$. Transport this equality through the germ isomorphism $S_{\mathfrak p}\cong A$ to obtain $\dim A=d$.

Each germ isomorphism of local rings carries the unique maximal ideal onto the unique maximal ideal (units, and therefore nonunits, are preserved in both directions). It consequently carries every power of that ideal onto the corresponding power, and induces mutually inverse quotient-ring maps at each level. Apply these quotient maps coordinatewise to compatible sequences in the definition of adic completion. The inverse germ maps give inverse maps of compatible sequences. This supplies the asserted isomorphisms $\widehat A\cong\widehat{S_{\mathfrak p}}$ and $\widehat B\cong\widehat{T_{\mathfrak q}}$.
